# crashapi

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/crashapi)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=crashapi)

 [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/elipousson/crashapi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/elipousson/crashapi?branch=main)

The goal of the crashapi R package is to provide functions for downloading data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) [Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) API](https://crashviewer.nhtsa.dot.gov/crashviewer/CrashAPI/).

What is FARS? NHTSA explains: "The Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) contains data on all vehicle crashes in the United States that occur on a public roadway and involve a fatality."

## Installation

You can install the development version of crashapi using the pak package:

``` r
pak::pkg_install("elipousson/crashapi")
```

## Background

### Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) API support

Supported APIs for this package include:

-   [x] Get Crash List Information
-   [X] Get Crash Details
-   [x] Get Crashes By Location
-   [X] Get Crashes By Vehicle
-   [x] Get Summary Counts
-   [x] Get Variables and Get Variable Attributes
-   [x] Get FARS Data By Year
-   [X] Get Crashes By Occupant

Most of these APIs support XML, JSV, CSV, and JSON output formats. This package only uses JSON with the exception of `get_fars_year()` (which supports downloading CSV files).

For reference, this package also includes a list of terms and NHTSA technical definitions in `fars_terms` and a list of variable labels in `fars_vars_labels`.

The FARS API currently provides access to data from 2010 to 2024. The [NHTSA website](https://www-fars.nhtsa.dot.gov/Help/helplinks.aspx) also provides additional information on the release data and version status for the FARS data files available through the API:

| Data Year | File Version | Release Date      |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 2010      | Final        | December 11, 2012 |
| 2011      | Final        | November 13, 2013 |
| 2012      | Final        | December 12, 2013 |
| 2013      | Final        | December 14, 2014 |
| 2014      | Final        | December 18, 2015 |
| 2015      | Final        | December 16, 2016 |
| 2016      | Final        | December 14, 2017 |
| 2017      | Final        | December 18, 2018 |
| 2018      | Final        | June 24, 2021     |
| 2019      | Final        | March 2, 2022     |
| 2020      | Final        | April 3, 2023     |
| 2021      | Final        | April 1, 2024     |
| 2022      | Final        | April 8, 2025     |
| 2023      | Final        | April 1, 2026     |
| 2024      | Annual       | April 1, 2026     |

### Changes to the sex variable

According to the [Data Index terminations tracker](https://dataindex.us/terminations-tracker), in February 2025 NHTSA renamed the person-level gender variable to "Sex" and recoded its third response value to "Not Reported", removing the non-binary category from published FARS data files. The [FARS 2022 release notes](https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/2022/FARS2022%20Release%20Notes.txt) confirm that on February 11, 2025, NHTSA replaced attribute 3 with attribute 8 (Not Reported), updating 22 records in the PERSON table and 1 record in the PBTYPE table. See [OMB ICR 202503-2127-008](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAViewICR?ref_nbr=202503-2127-008) and the Williams Institute report [Removal of SOGI from Federal Data Collections (Feb 2026)](https://williamsinstitute.law.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/Federal-SOGI-Data-Collection-Feb-2026.pdf) for more information.

Data now returned by the CrashAPI codes `SEX` as 1 (Male), 2 (Female), 8 (Not Reported), or 9 (Reported as Unknown) for all years, so people previously recorded as non-binary now appear as "Not Reported".

### Additional data access functionality

The `get_fars_zip()` function can be used to access FARS data files from 1975 to 2024 that are not available via the API but are available for download through [the NHTSA File Downloads site](https://www.nhtsa.gov/file-downloads?p=nhtsa/downloads/FARS/) as zipped CSV or SAS files. Zipped CSV files are converted to parquet files and cached in the user cache directory (see `tools::R_user_dir()`) so the data only needs to be downloaded once. This site also provides extensive technical documentation on coding and use of the FARS data files.

The `get_crss_zip()` function works the same way for data files from the [Crash Report Sampling System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/crash-data-systems/crash-report-sampling-system) (CRSS) from 2016 to 2024. CRSS is a national sample of police-reported crashes of all severities (not only fatal crashes) that replaced the General Estimates System (GES) in 2016. Since CRSS is a sample, national estimates should use the sampling weights and survey design variables described in the CRSS Analytical User's Manual, and the data does not include crash locations.

Earlier data along with data from the [General Estimates System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/national-automotive-sampling-system-nass/nass-general-estimates-system) (GES) / [Crash Report Sampling System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/crash-data-systems/crash-report-sampling-system) (CRSS) is also available through the [Fatality and Injury Reporting System Tool](https://cdan.dot.gov/query) (FIRST).

## Examples

```{r}
library(crashapi)
library(ggplot2)
```

Use `get_fars()` to get a FARS data table (e.g. accident, person, or vehicle) for one or more states, a county, and one or more years. Data for a state from 2010 onwards comes from the CrashAPI and national data or data before 2010 comes from the cached zipped data files.

```{r get_fars}
# Get the person table for Baltimore City, MD for 2022
md_people <-
  get_fars(
    state = "MD",
    county = "Baltimore city",
    year = 2022,
    type = "person"
  )

head(md_people[, c("ST_CASE", "VEH_NO", "PER_NO", "AGE", "SEXNAME", "INJ_SEVNAME")])
```

You can set geometry to TRUE to convert the accident table into an `sf` object for mapping.

```{r map_fars_crashes}
crashes_sf <-
  get_fars(
    state = "NC",
    county = "Wake County",
    year = 2018:2021,
    geometry = TRUE
  )

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"))
wake_co <- sf::st_transform(nc[nc$NAME == "Wake", ], 4326)

# Map crashes
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = wake_co,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = sf::st_crop(crashes_sf, wake_co),
    aes(color = VE_TOTAL),
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

National data or data before 2010 is downloaded and cached the first time it is used:

```{r get_fars_national, eval = FALSE}
# Get the national vehicle table for 2024
get_fars(year = 2024, type = "vehicle")

# Get the accident table for Maryland for 2005
get_fars(state = "MD", year = 2005)
```

The CrashAPI and FARS zipped CSV files from 2015 onwards include `…NAME` columns with decoded values for coded variables. For older FARS data, `get_fars()` adds these columns using `decode_fars()`, which can also decode CRSS data from `get_crss_zip()` (using `source = "CRSS"`). Both use value labels from `fars_value_labels()`, which are built from the SAS format files NHTSA publishes with each year of data. Value labels can change between years:

```{r fars_value_labels}
inj_sev <- fars_value_labels(
  year = c(1985, 2024),
  table = "person",
  variable = "INJ_SEV"
)

inj_sev[, c("year", "code", "value")]
```

CRSS data files can be downloaded and cached with `get_crss_zip()`:

```{r get_crss_zip, eval = FALSE}
# Get all CRSS tables for 2024
crss_2024 <- get_crss_zip(year = 2024)

# Estimate the number of police-reported crashes using the sampling weight
sum(crss_2024$accident$WEIGHT)
```

Other CrashAPI endpoints are available through specific functions. For example, you can use `get_fars_summary()` to access state-level summary data on crash and fatality counts.

```{r get_fars_summary}
# Get summary crash count and fatality count data for Maryland from 2010 to 2021
md_summary <- get_fars_summary(state = "MD", year = 2010:2021)

ggplot(md_summary, aes(x = CaseYear, y = TotalFatalCounts)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_line(color = "red", group = 1) +
  theme_minimal()
```

You can list crashes and filter by the number of vehicles involved with `get_fars_crash_list()`.

```{r get_fars_crash_list}
# Get fatal crashes in New York state from 2019 with 5 to 10 vehicles
get_fars_crash_list(state = "NY", year = 2019, vehicles = c(5, 10))
```

If you call `get_fars_crashes()` with details set to TRUE, additional information from `get_fars_cases()` (including the crash date and time) is appended to the crash data frame.

```{r get_fars_crashes}
# Get fatal crashes for Anne Arundel County, MD for 2019 and append details
crashes_detailed <-
  get_fars_crashes(
    state = "MD",
    county = "Anne Arundel County",
    year = 2019,
    details = TRUE
  )

# Show 10 fatal crashes at random
dplyr::slice_sample(crashes_detailed, n = 10)
```

## Related packages and projects

-   [rfars](https://github.com/s87jackson/rfars) aims to "simplify the process of analyzing FARS data" by providing access to FARS downloads and preprocessed data back to 2015.
-   [stats19](https://github.com/ropensci/stats19) "provides functions for downloading and formatting road crash data" from "the UK's official road traffic casualty database, STATS19."
-   [njtr1](https://github.com/gavinrozzi/njtr1): "An R interface to New Jersey traffic crash data reported on form NJTR-1."
-   [wisdotcrashdatabase](https://github.com/jacciz/wisdotcrashdatabase): "A package used for internal WisDOT crash database pulls and analysis."
-   [nzcrash](https://github.com/nacnudus/nzcrash): "An R package to distribute New Zealand crash data in a convenient form."
-   [GraphHopper Open Traffic Collection](https://github.com/graphhopper/open-traffic-collection): "Collections of URLs pointing to traffic information portals which contain open data or at least data which is free to use."
-   [Open Crash Data Index](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rmn6GbHNkfWLLDEEmA87iuy2yHdh7hBybCTZiQJEY0k/edit?usp=sharing): A Google Sheet listing a range of city, county, regional and state sources for crash data including non-injury crashes as well as the fatal crashes available through the FARS API. Contributions for crash data from other U.S. cities and states are welcome.
